title: Starry, Starry Night
caption: Telescopes along the road at La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A dense scattering of stars fills the sky above the road to ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile's Atacama Desert, lined with a variety of telescopes. The Danish 1.54-meter telescope stands in the foreground, the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope beyond it, and, furthest back, ESO's New Technology Telescope (NTT).

The Danish telescope is at work, and it has made many discoveries, including the afterglows of short gamma-ray bursts, which are probably the result of two neutron stars colliding. The 2.2-meter telescope also hunts these afterglows with its GROND instrument, flagging them for larger telescopes to follow up.

The NTT may look like a speck, but it made key advances. Big mirrors sag under their own weight and need constant adjustment to stay sharp. The NTT was the first telescope to make these corrections on the fly, keeping watch on a reference star. Called active optics, the method is now widely used in large professional telescopes.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph at ESO's La Silla Observatory, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A camera exposure can gather far more light than the eye, so the sky may look more densely packed with stars than it would to someone on the road.

explore: Besides GROND, the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope also carries a spectrograph, plus a wide-field camera that has produced many fine pictures of the sky.
alt: A star-filled sky above a road lined with telescopes, one in the foreground and others further back.
